tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תְּפִלָּה לִסְגֻלַּת אִשִּׁים
Prayer for a practice of divine contemplation, attributed to a Rabbi Mosheh (as found in Leiden Or. 4779, et al)

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer for a practice of divine contemplation, attributed to a Rabbi Mosheh (as found in Leiden Or. 4779, et al)

tei:lg.tei:l: A large paper codex (initially 525 folios, later supplemented with folios 324–325); written in a script tending toward the Spanish style, with additional Karaite Eastern script—partly bold, partly smaller (see the sample from fols. 256 and 288, where the scribe is Isaac Tishbi, etc., see under item 19). The early owners identify themselves as Jehuda Gur b. Menachem (רכיצי 1), (the monogram is clearer here), from whom in the year 1646 the codex was purchased by Abishai b. Josef Zaddik for 41⁄2 silver pieces (כספים); and finally, in the year 1660, it was purchased for 4 silver pieces by Moses Jerushalmi from כרשולה, the wife, and Shemariah, the son of Abishai Zaddik.

11) (f. 150) תפלת הרב רבי׳ משה זצ״ל, Prayer of R. Mosheh [Maimonides], incip.: תפלה לסגולת אישים, למבחר אנשים, לחכמי חרשים, לנבוני לחשים, לחופשי טמונים, למפענחי צפונים, לדורשי יש אין לפניו אין, אשר לא תשורנו עין, והבורא הכל יסור היסודות, וסוד הסודות, שמו עצמו, ועצמו שמו. It is rather a philosophical contemplation, ending in the form of a prayer, (ib. ואשעה בחקיך תמיד. ברוך אתה יו׳ שומע תפלה אמן), a work worthy of this author, to whom it is also attributed in the Paris manuscript no. 285 (Carmoly, עקטאן p. 4 no. 5), and who composed other works of this kind (see the Catalogue [Catalogus librorum hebraeorum in bibliotheca Bodleiana] column 1868, compare columns 2442, 2462). Ours will be published elsewhere.”

tei:note.tei:p: Rosner notes this is likely a deprecated shelf mark for Bnf Ms. Hébreu 873
